items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: I think the fact that I was a musician had a lot to do with Grove and my ability to write about music

ctx.x: Do you think that the fact that you’re a musician contributed to the fact that this is so important to you?

Sure. I’m not sure how to answer that question. I mean I was obsessed with jazz, so interesting question. I’m pausing here to think that the reason it’s so important to me may have — I think the fact that I was a musician had a lot to do with Grove and my ability to write about music and decide if comments about the music were B.S. or not. But I think what you just asked has more to do with me being a kind of nerdy intellectual. And that it was important to me for those reasons, because there is to my mind this…

Well said. You reminded me that when I was fortunate to interview Phil Woods he was talking about himself and he said, “Well I’m not an innovator, I’m a craftsman. You know, I learned from of course Charlie Parker and others.” But he didn’t consider himself to be doing anything really innovative. Perhaps he added his own flavor to it but it sort of goes to what you’re talking about. Who are the fountainheads of these musical styles?
